title: Shared definitions
description: The types the methods and events of shapelogic_engine share (decision 0012).

ShapeId.description: A shape, stable while the document is open.

ProblemId.description: A problem; also names its solve and its analysis.

RodSetId.description: A stacking puzzle's rod set (a board), stable while the document is open.

SolutionId.description: A saved solution, unique within its problem.

AssemblyExplorerHandle.description: An assembly explorer opened by explore.openAssembly.

MovementExplorerHandle.description: A movement explorer opened by explore.openMovements.

Revision.description: The document's revision; every change increments it.

Changed.description: The result of a mutating call: the revision after it (unchanged when the call changed nothing).

Rgb.description: A colour, #rrggbb (the engine writes lower case).

Cell.description: A cell [x, y, z] in the grid's own coordinates.

Point2.description: A point [x, y] of a layer drawing, y up.

Grid.description: The grid of a puzzle, fixed for its life.

Solver.description: Complete (ShapeLogic), or Fast (Crowell): Andrew Crowell's take-apart.

SlidingSolver.description: How far a sliding puzzle's search may go: 250,000 arrangements, 1,000,000, or no limit (the full search keeps its older levels on disk and spreads each over threads; the default).

StackingSolver.description: The Stacking Solver (the fewest rod transfers: the Panex search whenever the puzzle fits it, which pauses, carries on and saves itself, else a search of its own) or the Panex Solver (the Panex search alone, for rod sets with Panex columns; a puzzle it cannot take is refused with its reason).

SolveState.description: decision 0004; 'stopping' is an active state with a stop requested (SolveProgress.stage).

SolveStage.description: What a solve is doing; search is a sliding puzzle's search from a start to the goal, or a stacking puzzle's from its start stacking (SolveProgress.searched, searchDepth, searchTraced, panexSearch).

ProblemState.description: What the problem holds of solving: nothing, a started solve (maybe paused), a finished one, or counts lost by an edit.

CellTool.description: The grid editor's tools; paint changes only the colour of non-empty cells.

ShapeTask.description: A button of the tool tabs; what the numbered ones do depends on the grid (shape.taskSet gives each one's group and label).

MeshStyle.description: The 3D view's bevelled cells, the same closed with the wire-frame faces flagged, flat faces with edge lines, or the STL export's mesh at the view's own parameters (the original's "Draw pieces like STL export": gap 0.02 and bevel 0.05 of a cell with the interior chamfers, the sphere grid's balls at two recursions; closed; the flat mesh where the mesher fails). The STL style's cell faces carry the checker flag, as the others', and bevels are flagged 16; the original drew it in one colour. It is made with the Manifold library on the prism, rhombic and tetra-octa grids and takes a while for large shapes (seconds in a release build).

SolutionsVersion.description: A counter the problem moves on every change of its saved list (a solution added, removed, re-sorted or edited), kept while the document is open: solution.page and solve.solutionsAdded carry it, so pages read at one value belong together and a client knows when to page again.

SortBy.description: Where a new solution goes in the saved list while solving: the original's sort-by choice.

ArrayRef.description: A typed array inside a binary frame, little-endian, its offset a multiple of 4.

Frame.description: A binary frame sent before the reply (decision 0012): its number, its size, and the arrays in it.

MeshFrame.description: A drawing mesh: arrays positions and normals (f32, xyz per vertex), indices (u32, three per triangle), and per triangle voxel (u32, the cell index x + X*(y + Y*z)), voxelFace (i32, its side, -1 for bevels and gaps), flags (u32, FaceFlag bits: 1 light checker colour, 2 variable mark, 4 the variable marker face, 8 wire frame, 16 bevel, 32 gap, 128 inside), colour (u8, colour number, 0 none; padded), polygon (u32); and edgeLines (f32, two points per line, flat style only).

hotspot.description: The hotspot of the shape in the mesh's orientation, in grid coordinates: an assembly puts it on a Placement's cell, so the mesh is drawn moved by the cell minus the hotspot (in mesh units: the grid's cell spacing).

RodSet.description: A stacking puzzle's board: a row of rods and the rules of a move (the original's rod set; its fields as the Rods panel showed them).

label.description: R1, R2, ... by place (shown as 'R1 - name' with a name).

rodCount.description: How many rods (the pocket column not counted).

rods.description: The rods of a stack map: rodCount, and one more with the pocket column (the last; it stands left of rod 1).

growHeight.description: Grow to the height of all pieces: a rod holds every disc of the problem.

definedHeight.description: Defined height: the discs a rod holds when it does not grow.

sizeMatters.description: Disc size matters - no large on small (equal sizes stack); Panex columns ignore it.

distanceMatters.description: Disc can only move over 1 rod: to a neighbouring rod only.

panexColumns.description: Panex Style Columns: a disc of size s sits at most s places below the top, in any order; one disc more may wait raised into the bridge, blocking moves that pass over it.

pocketColumn.description: Add pocket column (with Panex columns): an extra rod beside rod 1 that holds any disc.

pocketHeight.description: The discs the pocket column holds.

outsideChannel.description: Extra outside channel (with Panex columns and three rods or more): the first and last rods are joined outside the bridge.

DiscRef.description: One copy of a disc on a rod: the shape, and which of its copies (from 0).

shape.description: Null for a shape the file names that the puzzle does not have (only an edited file; setupError says so).

Stacks.description: Each rod of a stack map, its discs bottom to top; rods past the board's count are kept while they hold discs.

BoardLayout.description: Where the rods and the discs of a stacking stand (the original's layoutBoard), in cells: what the 3D view draws around the discs' meshes.

rodCount.description: The rods drawn, the pocket column included.

rodX.description: x of each rod, in the stack map's order (the pocket last, standing left of rod 1).

rodHeights.description: The drawn height of each rod; the pocket column is shorter.

panex.description: Panex columns: drawn with a V that narrows to the bottom.

pocket.description: The last rod is the pocket column, drawn as a plain peg.

maxSize.description: The largest disc size, so the V stays inside the rod spacing.

discs.description: Each disc of the problem (its pieces: parts, then copies) and the cell its hotspot (its centre) stands on; null for a disc on no rod. Empty for a rod set drawn alone.

name.description: A start/goal shape's is the user's part (shown as '(START/GOAL n) name').

colour.description: The shape's own colour, or null for the default one.

startGoal.description: A sliding puzzle's start/goal shape: its number n (sliding.json); null for any other shape.

disc.description: A stacking puzzle's disc: its size, the radius, which the size rule compares (stacking.setDiscSize); null for any other shape.

discColour.description: A stacking puzzle's disc: the palette colour of its first coloured cell, which the 3D view draws the disc in (the original's diskTint); null for a disc without one, or for any other shape.

rodSet.description: A stacking problem's board (stacking.setProblemRodSet, the original's Set Start/Goal Rods); null for none and on other grids.

pieces.description: The number of pieces (the parts' maxima summed).

Snapshot.description: Everything a front end shows of the document's lists.

path.description: The file it was opened from or last saved to.

solving.description: A solve or an analysis is active: shapes and lists are frozen (decision 0011).

rodSets.description: A stacking puzzle's boards (at least one); empty on other grids.

notice.description: What opening the file changed, to tell the user (the original's load message). Only in the result of document.open, document.openBytes and solve.importPaused, and only when there is something to tell.

ShapeInfo.description: A row of the status window.

identicalMirror.description: An earlier shape it is identical to, mirrors allowed.

symmetry.description: The symmetry group number, when the grid's tables know it.

statusLine.description: The original's status line for the shape.

required.description: A sliding piece with a start or goal on the problem's start/goal shape: its count follows them (problem.setPieceCount refuses to change it; the range and all-pieces commands leave it).

SolverSettings.description: The Solver tab's settings stored with a problem (saved in the file, the original's names; the front end decides what they mean). Settings of other versions are kept as strings. These names are the file's and stay: SolveOptions uses the API's (deepSymmetry is completeRotations, strictColors is strictColours, justLevels is justLevels; nestedSlides, partialNested and highMemory are sliding's nestedSlides, partialNested and highMemory, solverType fast, deep or full its solver). highMemory belongs to the stacking solvers too.

rodSet.description: A stacking problem's board (stacking.setProblemRodSet, the original's Set Start/Goal Rods); null for none and on other grids.

colourRules.description: The allowed pairs: a piece cell of colour 'piece' may sit on a result cell of colour 'result'.

savedPosition.description: A paused search position is stored (solve.continue carries on from it).

oneOf.description: A stacking problem's discs on each rod of its board at the start and at the goal (stacking.json).

FitStats.description: Whether the pieces can fill the result (the fit summary).

SolveOptions.description: What a solve does (the solve thread's flags); a missing field takes the engine's setting or the default.

disassemble.description: Take each assembly apart; only those that come apart are solutions.

checkRotations.description: Try 90 degree turns while taking apart.

justLevels.description: Keep the level summary of each take-apart, not its moves.

completeRotations.description: The thorough rotation check (the original's deep symmetry check).

reduce.description: Drop placements that can never be part of an assembly first (default true).

keepAtMost.description: Keep at most this many solutions; 0 all (default 10).

keepEach.description: Unsorted, keep every n-th (0 and 1: each).

threads.description: Assembly and take-apart together; 0 every hardware thread.

SlidingOptions.description: A sliding puzzle's search (the solve thread's sliding flags). A sliding solve always keeps mirrored and rotated starts and matches colours strictly (the start locks), whatever the brick fields say; disassemble (the GUI's Find Solutions) searches each start to the goal; solver, checkRotations, justLevels and sortBy play no part (a path found goes at the end of the list). Where a full search keeps its levels is the engine's setting (slideFolder, slideDiskGB).

nestedSlides.description: A piece may carry what is nested in its outline (Allow Nested Slides).

partialNested.description: And what is partly nested in it (Allow Partially Nested); implies nestedSlides.

highMemory.description: Hold up to half the machine's memory in arrangements, not about 2 GB (Enable High Memory).

StackingOptions.description: A stacking puzzle's search (the solve thread's stacking flags). A stacking solve has no assembler and no take-apart: one search from the start stacking to the goal, whose path is the one solution (its assembly the start stacking). disassemble (the GUI's Find Solutions) or justCount must be on; threads count; the brick fields play no part. solve.prepare is refused (unsupported), and so is solve.savePoint: the search saves itself. Where it is saved is the engine's setting (panexFolder, panexDiskGB).

solver.description: Default: the Panex Solver for a problem on Panex columns, else the Stacking Solver (the original's menu offered only that one).

highMemory.description: Hold up to half the machine's memory in stackings (Enable High Memory).

autosave.description: The Panex search saves itself every 20 minutes (default true); off, only when it stops (the GUI's Autosave box).

overall.description: The whole solve, 0 to 1; never goes back during a run.

activity.description: The original's status text (empty in the search stage, which the original GUI told as 'Sliding search, N moves deep. Scanned N arrangements.', 'Panex search, N moves deep. Found N stackings.', 'Panex search, tracing the path. Traced N of M moves.' or 'Stacking search. Scanned N stackings.').

searched.description: The sliding search under way: the arrangements it has visited; the stacking search: the stackings it has searched (found, for the Panex search).

searchDepth.description: How many moves deep a full sliding search is (0 before its first level, and for the other searches); how many moves deep both ends of the Panex search are together.

searchTraced.description: Once the ends of the Panex search have met: how many moves of the path are traced back (of searchDepth); 0 before.

panexSearch.description: The Panex Solver runs (its words: 'Panex search'), not the Stacking Solver ('Stacking search').

SolveFailure.description: Why a run ended in error.

assembler.description: The preparation's or the saved position's error; null for an internal error.

param.description: The piece or number the error names.

Placement.description: Where a piece is in an assembly.

piece.description: The problem's piece number (pieces are numbered part by part).

index.description: Its place in the saved list.

assembly.description: The assembly number (the original shows it plus one).

solution.description: The solution number (0 without a disassembly).

disassembly.description: The moves are stored; only the level summary; not taken apart (or found not to come apart).

moves.description: A stacking solution's: its rod transfers (each three frames of its path), as the original counted them; steps and movesText the same.

MovementNode.description: A position of a movement explorer's tree.

parent.description: The root is its own parent.

label.description: The direction and the pieces moved, e.g. 'x: S1, S2.2'; empty for the root.
